```{r,message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

Recalling that for continuous time (t can be any real positive number)

$N_t=N_0e^{r_m t}$

\$log(Nt) = log(N0) + rm \* t

and for a annual time step (t is integer years or days)

$N_t=N_0\lambda^t$

Where

$\lambda=e^{r_m}$

### Neal: Introduction to Population Biology question 4.1.

Each individual of an annual plant species produces on average ten seeds. (a) Starting with a single individual, what will be the population size after 6 years, assuming all the seeds survive to produce adult plants the following generation? (b) A new variety of the plant produces 5 per cent more seeds, i.e. 10.5 seeds on average. What will be the potential number of offspring after 6 years from a single individual?

Annual plant, so

Nt=N0 lamda t

t=6 years

N0= starting population = 1 seed

N\[t+1\]=N\[0\] \* lamda

lamda = rate of change between the population of the first year and the population of the following years

In this example, lamda = 10

N\[t+1\]= (1\*10)\^6 = 10\^6

N\[t+1\]= (1\*10.5)\^6

10.5\^6

### Neal: Introduction to Population Biology question 4.2.

\(a\) The Norway rat breeds continuously and has an estimated rate of natural increase (rm) of 0.0143 per day. A small number invade a garbage dump where living conditions are ideal. How long will it take the population to double in size?

When population doubles, Nt/N0 = 2 = e\^rmt

log(2) = rmt

t= log (2) / rm

t = log(2) /0.0143

2 = (1 \* 0.0143)\^t

### Neal: Introduction to Population Biology question 4.5.

A population increases fivefold over a 4-week period. What is the value of $\lambda$ per day, assuming exponential growth?

4\*7 = 28 days = t

Nt/N0 = lambda\^t = 5

5 = lambda\^28

5\^(1/28) = lambda

lambda = 1.059164

t=28

lambda = e\^rm

log(5) = rmt

rm = log (5) / 28

lambd
